amendments.normalized_body: In `reproduction_factors.rs:1505-1512`, the neglected-tank assertion was tightened from `<= initial_total + 5` to `<= initial_total`. The alternative branch (`+ 3 <= neglected_peak_population`) catches the case where breeding temporarily raises the population before stress mortality reverses it. However, if the model is retuned such that early breeding adds a few shrimp but peak tracking misses the exact peak (e.g., peak occurs mid-day between snapshot checks), the test could become flaky. Consider adding a small tolerance (e.g., `<= initial_total + 2`) to the first branch to absorb minor early-breeding growth without relying solely on peak tracking.

In `e2e_validation_suite.rs:1034-1037`, the VS-07 bare-bottom arm uses `seeded_state_with_full_overrides(SimSeed(7307), "medium_planted", bare_overrides)` — note the scenario template is `"medium_planted"` even though `plant_selection` is `None`. While this works because the overrides strip plants, using `"medium_planted"` as the template name is misleading for future maintainers reading the test. Consider introducing a more neutral template or adding a comment explaining why `medium_planted` is used as the base for a bare-bottom, plantless arm.

Track `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs` in version control. The whole new regression suite currently exists only as an untracked file (`crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1`), so none of these alkalinity tests will ship or run in CI when this change is committed.

Unify the nitrification alkalinity default across construction paths. `ProcessParams::default()` now uses `NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N` at `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:338`, but preset-backed states still come from a separate hard-coded literal in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1018-1019`. Wire the preset default through the same constant (or add a regression asserting equality) so default-built tanks and preset/scenario tanks do not continue to simulate slightly different alkalinity depletion.

Fix the alkalinity assertion diagnostics in `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:472-475` and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:495-503`. The new `Element::Alkalinity` path compares meq values, but the per-system and per-tick panic text still labels those values as `mg`, so a failing alkalinity check will report the wrong unit.
